approaches.name: Self-attention
approaches.problem: Each token needs a way to fetch relevant information from any other token in the same sequence, including distant words, variables, names, or clauses.
approaches.how_it_works: Turn every token vector into a query, key, and value. The query says what this token is looking for. The key says what each other token offers. Dot products between queries and keys become attention weights after softmax. The token then receives a weighted sum of value vectors, so its new representation contains information from the selected context.
approaches.why_it_matters: This replaces a narrow left-to-right memory with direct content-based lookup across the whole context, which is the central operation behind transformer language models.
approaches.failure_mode: The cost grows quickly with context length, and the model can attend strongly to irrelevant or misleading tokens if the learned match is wrong.

approaches.name: Transformer block stacking
approaches.problem: One attention lookup can mix context, but language understanding often requires several rounds of relation building and nonlinear feature changes.
approaches.how_it_works: A block runs attention to exchange information across tokens, then a feed-forward network to transform each token independently. Residual connections preserve earlier information while adding updates, and normalization keeps vector scales stable. Stacking many blocks lets later layers operate on relations built by earlier layers.
approaches.why_it_matters: Depth lets the model move from raw token patterns to richer features such as reference, syntax, topic, code structure, and answer-relevant context.
approaches.failure_mode: Very deep stacks can become expensive, unstable, or hard to serve if normalization, residual layout, memory, and parallelism are poorly designed.

approaches.name: Positional encoding
approaches.problem: Self-attention compares token content but does not naturally know whether one token came first, later, nearby, or far away.
approaches.how_it_works: Attach position information to each token, either by adding learned or sinusoidal position vectors, using relative position terms in attention, or rotating query and key vectors with position-dependent transformations. This makes order and distance visible during query-key matching.
approaches.why_it_matters: Order changes meaning. The model needs position to understand syntax, chronology, code structure, and long-context references.
approaches.failure_mode: A position scheme can fail outside its trained context length or make extrapolation brittle when documents become longer than training examples.

approaches.name: Causal masking
approaches.problem: A next-token model must learn from past context only; if it can see future tokens during training, the task becomes dishonest and generation will not match training.
approaches.how_it_works: Before softmax, add a mask to the attention score matrix so token i cannot attend to token j when j is in the future. Illegal scores become effectively negative infinity, so their softmax weights become zero.
approaches.why_it_matters: The mask defines the allowed information flow and makes next-token training match real generation, where future tokens do not exist yet.
approaches.failure_mode: A wrong mask can leak answers, block valid context, break packed sequences, or silently train a model that behaves differently at inference time.

approaches.name: Next-token pretraining
approaches.problem: The model needs a training objective that can be produced from raw text at huge scale without humans labeling every example.
approaches.how_it_works: For each position in a text sequence, give the model the previous tokens and train it to assign high probability to the actual next token. Cross-entropy turns that probability into a loss. Repeating this over many domains forces the model to encode grammar, facts, code patterns, style, and common reasoning moves.
approaches.why_it_matters: It converts ordinary text into dense supervision: every token position becomes a lesson, which is why large models can be trained on broad unlabeled corpora.
approaches.failure_mode: The objective rewards likely continuations, not guaranteed truth, helpfulness, or safety; a model can be fluent and wrong.

approaches.name: Token-to-logit pipeline
approaches.problem: Text must be turned into numbers the model can process and then turned back into a probability over possible next text pieces.
approaches.how_it_works: A tokenizer maps text to token ids. An embedding table maps ids to vectors. Transformer blocks update those vectors with context. The final hidden vector is multiplied by an output matrix to produce logits over the vocabulary. Softmax converts logits into probabilities used for loss or sampling.
approaches.why_it_matters: This pipeline is the concrete path from raw text to trainable neural computation and back to generated language.
approaches.failure_mode: Bad tokenization, limited context, poor calibration, or bad decoding settings can damage behavior even when the transformer itself is strong.

approaches.name: Large-scale pretraining system
approaches.problem: A simple loss does not automatically become a good model; large training runs can waste compute, collapse, memorize, or learn bad data patterns.
approaches.how_it_works: Build a curated data mixture, sample batches, run forward passes, compute next-token loss, backpropagate gradients, update weights with a scheduled optimizer, and track validation by domain. The system also needs checkpointing, data audits, deduplication, and hardware parallelism so progress is stable and measurable.
approaches.why_it_matters: The training system is what turns the transformer architecture into a capable model; data and optimization choices often matter as much as the block design.
approaches.failure_mode: Data bugs, duplicate benchmarks, unstable learning rates, bad batch construction, or weak validation can produce a costly model that looks good on the wrong evidence.

approaches.name: Efficient scaling
approaches.problem: More parameters and more tokens usually improve capability, but training and serving cost can become too high.
approaches.how_it_works: Use scaling-law estimates to allocate compute among model size and data size. Use efficiency ideas such as mixture-of-experts, sparse activation, better kernels, and parallel training so only part of the model or hardware path is active for each token where possible.
approaches.why_it_matters: Efficient scaling lets teams buy more useful capacity per unit of compute and makes large models practical to train and serve.
approaches.failure_mode: Routing imbalance, communication overhead, expert collapse, or serving complexity can erase the efficiency gain.

approaches.name: Supervised fine-tuning
approaches.problem: A pretrained model may continue text instead of following instructions, and it may not know the answer style expected in a user-facing assistant.
approaches.how_it_works: Train the model on prompt-response demonstrations. The prompt is provided as context and the loss is usually applied to the desired answer tokens. This increases the probability of the demonstrated response style, format, and task behavior.
approaches.why_it_matters: It teaches the model the interaction contract: read the request, answer directly, use the desired format, and follow task-specific conventions.
approaches.failure_mode: The model can overfit demonstration style, become too narrow, copy mistakes in the examples, or lose some base-model breadth if tuning is too aggressive.

approaches.name: Preference tuning
approaches.problem: Many qualities such as helpfulness, clarity, safety, and tone are easier to compare between two answers than to encode as one exact target answer.
approaches.how_it_works: Collect pairs of answers to the same prompt where one is chosen and one is rejected. Train a reward model, run RL with a KL constraint, or use a direct preference loss that raises the relative probability of chosen answers over rejected answers.
approaches.why_it_matters: It shapes behavior beyond imitation and lets the model prefer better answers when many fluent completions are possible.
approaches.failure_mode: The model can optimize the preference proxy through verbosity, flattery, over-refusal, or style tricks that win comparisons without improving truth.

approaches.name: Reasoning traces
approaches.problem: Hard tasks often require intermediate state, but a final answer hides the steps that led there.
approaches.how_it_works: Let the model generate intermediate text such as a plan, derivation, scratch work, or code outline before the final answer. The trace remains in context, so later tokens can attend to earlier work and build on it. Training can imitate reference traces or prefer traces that lead to correct outcomes.
approaches.why_it_matters: A visible workspace can make multi-step computation more reliable and gives training or evaluation systems something to inspect before the final answer.
approaches.failure_mode: The trace can be unfaithful, padded, circular, or persuasive while the underlying answer is still wrong.

approaches.name: Verifier-guided reasoning
approaches.problem: One sampled solution may be wrong, and final correctness alone gives weak feedback about which path was good.
approaches.how_it_works: Generate several candidate traces or answers, score them with a verifier, unit test, equation checker, human label, or process reward model, then select the best candidate or train the model toward higher-scoring steps and answers.
approaches.why_it_matters: It turns extra inference or checking compute into higher reliability on tasks where mistakes are common.
approaches.failure_mode: A weak verifier becomes a new target to game and may reward superficial signs of correctness rather than valid reasoning.

approaches.name: Retrieval-augmented generation
approaches.problem: The model’s weights may not contain current, private, rare, or exact information needed for an answer.
approaches.how_it_works: Split documents into chunks, embed chunks and queries into vectors, retrieve the nearest relevant chunks, and place those chunks into the model context with instructions to answer from them. The language model then conditions on retrieved evidence instead of relying only on memory.
approaches.why_it_matters: It lets a fixed model use fresh or private knowledge without retraining and gives answers a source trail that can be checked.
approaches.failure_mode: Retrieval can return irrelevant, stale, adversarial, or incomplete chunks; the model can also ignore good evidence or overtrust bad evidence.

approaches.name: Tool-calling agent loop
approaches.problem: Some tasks require exact computation, external side effects, file edits, searches, or tests that text generation alone cannot perform reliably.
approaches.how_it_works: Give the model a set of tools with schemas. The model chooses a tool call, arguments are validated, the tool runs, and the observation is appended to context. The model repeats observe, decide, act, and observe until it can answer or stop.
approaches.why_it_matters: It turns an LLM from a text generator into a controller for a bounded work process, letting it calculate, inspect, retrieve, execute, and verify.
approaches.failure_mode: The loop can call the wrong tool, trust malicious output, leak sensitive data, spend too much money, or continue without a stopping condition.

approaches.name: Task-specific evaluation
approaches.problem: A general leaderboard score may not measure the behavior needed for a real product, research workflow, or safety case.
approaches.how_it_works: Define the actual task distribution, expected users, allowed evidence, and unacceptable failures. Build slices for common cases, edge cases, adversarial cases, and regressions. Measure correctness, grounding, safety, latency, cost, and reliability separately instead of collapsing everything into one vague score.
approaches.why_it_matters: It makes evaluation decision-relevant: the score tells whether the model works for the intended use, not merely whether it performs well on a public benchmark.
approaches.failure_mode: If the slices are too narrow, contaminated, or poorly labeled, evaluation can bless a model that fails in deployment.

approaches.name: Human and preference evaluation
approaches.problem: Some answer qualities, such as clarity, usefulness, and tone, cannot be fully captured by exact-match metrics.
approaches.how_it_works: Ask human raters or calibrated judge models to compare outputs using a rubric. Aggregate multiple judgments, check agreement, and separate dimensions such as factuality, helpfulness, style, safety, and citation faithfulness.
approaches.why_it_matters: It captures user-facing quality that automatic metrics miss and supplies data for preference tuning.
approaches.failure_mode: Judgments can be noisy, biased, expensive, rubric-sensitive, or gamed by answers that sound confident.

approaches.name: Pipeline-based paper reading
approaches.problem: New LLM papers often introduce names and demos that make the field look like disconnected tricks.
approaches.how_it_works: Place the method into the pipeline: tokenizer, embedding, position handling, attention, architecture, pretraining data, loss, post-training, retrieval, tools, reasoning, serving, or evaluation. Then compare the old and new computation at that location.
approaches.why_it_matters: It turns new work into a concrete modification of known machinery, which makes papers easier to understand and compare.
approaches.failure_mode: Some methods change several parts at once, so forcing them into one slot can hide the real source of improvement.

approaches.name: Bottleneck-first analysis
approaches.problem: It is easy to mistake a trend for progress if the bottleneck and tradeoff are not named.
approaches.how_it_works: Ask what pressure the method attacks, what object or objective it changes, what evidence would prove success, and what failure remains. Read ablations and deployment constraints before accepting the headline claim.
approaches.why_it_matters: This keeps attention on mechanism and consequence instead of demos, branding, or benchmark cherry-picking.
approaches.failure_mode: The stated bottleneck in a paper may not be the bottleneck in a real system, so the method can be technically valid but practically irrelevant.
